title: Telemetry pipeline retention: define eligible analytics tables, implement partition TTLs, validate reporting queries
creator: Logan Wright
project: Enterprise Security & Compliance Foundation — Retention controls + compliance reporting pack
content:
Context
We’re adding tenant-configurable retention controls and a baseline compliance reporting pack. For v1, telemetry/analytics retention needs to be enforceable (not just policy text) for a defined set of datasets. This ticket covers:
1) defining which analytics tables in the telemetry pipeline are eligible for retention enforcement in v1, and
2) implementing partition-level TTLs (or equivalent) for those tables, and
3) validating that existing reporting queries/dashboards continue to behave correctly as historical partitions are deleted.

This is explicitly NOT “full custom retention across every internal log stream.” We should focus on the analytics tables that show up in customer-facing Console dashboards and internal usage reporting, where predictable deletion semantics matter for enterprise security reviews.

Owners / reviewers
- DRI: Mei Lin
- Reviewer: Logan Wright
- Consulted: Nadia Rahman (metering), Caleb Johnson (ingestion), Sean Gallagher (SRE), Olga Petrov (GRC)

Current state (as of 2025-01-23)
- Primary analytics store: ClickHouse (cluster: ch-telemetry-prod, db: telemetry)
- Most high-volume tables are partitioned by event_date (Date) or bucketed by toYYYYMM(event_ts)
- Retention is inconsistent:
  - Some tables have manual drop-partition jobs (SRE cron) with coarse settings
  - Some are effectively “keep forever” (especially intermediate/derived tables)
- Console dashboards (cost/latency/error rates) query a mix of raw-ish event tables + daily aggregates. A number of queries assume “all history exists” and lack explicit time windows.

Decision: v1 eligibility scope
Eligible tables MUST meet all of:
- Partitioned on a date/time key (event_date or toYYYYMM(event_ts)) so we can safely TTL at partition granularity
- No customer-provided raw content (no prompts/responses)
- Used for customer-facing analytics OR compliance reporting evidence (usage/cost/latency summaries)
- Deletion does not break billing correctness (billing source-of-truth remains metering ledger)

Not eligible in v1:
- Any table that can contain raw inference payload content or debug dumps
- Any table required for billing reconciliation beyond the ledger’s retained window
- Any table not properly partitioned (would require expensive row-level deletes)
- SRE/internal infra log streams governed by separate standards/vendor limits

Proposed eligible tables (telemetry.*)
Raw / event-level (short retention, default 30d unless tenant policy says higher):
- telemetry.request_events_v2
  - Contains request metadata (tenant_id, model, region, status, token counts, latency buckets), NO prompt/response text
  - Partition: event_date
- telemetry.error_events_v1
  - Sanitized error events with error_class, status_code, service, route, tenant_id
  - Partition: event_date
- telemetry.trace_spans_v1 (if still used by Console; confirm)
  - NOTE: only if spans are sanitized and do not include payload attributes; otherwise exclude

Aggregates (longer retention, default 90d–365d depending on tier/policy):
- telemetry.daily_usage_agg_v1
  - Per-tenant/model/day token totals, request counts, cost estimates
  - Partition: day
- telemetry.latency_histogram_daily_v1
  - Per-tenant/route/day latency histograms
  - Partition: day
- telemetry.availability_slo_daily_v1
  - Per-tenant/day success rate + error class counts
  - Partition: day

Derived/supporting tables (validate individually):
- telemetry.route_catalog_snapshot_v1 (small; consider fixed 365d)
- telemetry.model_catalog_snapshot_v1 (small; consider fixed 365d)

Open question to close in implementation
- Which tables are directly configurable by tenant policy vs. fixed Redwood defaults?
  - Suggestion for v1: policy applies to “telemetry_eligible” category with guardrails, but we can implement as two buckets:
    - event-level tables: enforce min=7d, max=90d
    - aggregate tables: enforce min=30d, max=400d
  - This lines up with enterprise expectations without blowing up storage.

Implementation plan
A) Inventory + final eligibility list
- Cross-check against the working inventory sheet: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/security-and-compliance/data-inventory-and-retention-sources-sheet.json
- Confirm which tables are used by Console routes (ask Jada/Chloe for the query map if needed)
- Output: a concrete list with (table_name, partition_key, default_retention, min/max, owner, used_by)

B) Implement partition TTLs in ClickHouse
For each eligible table:
- Ensure partitioning is by a Date/Month expression compatible with TTL dropping whole parts.
- Add TTL in table definition (or ALTER TABLE … MODIFY TTL) using event_date/day column.
- Prefer TTL that deletes entire partitions/parts; avoid row-level TTL that triggers merges for massive tables.
- Example pattern (illustrative):
  - TTL event_date + INTERVAL {N} DAY DELETE
- Add settings to ensure TTL is enabled and predictable (coordinate with SRE for cluster-wide TTL merge settings).

C) Wire retention duration to policy evaluation (incremental)
- Phase 1 (this ticket): implement TTLs with configurable constants per environment (hosted prod/staging), behind a feature flag.
- Phase 2 (follow-up, if not feasible within this cycle): read the evaluated tenant policy (ENG-2912) and apply per-tenant retention.
  - Note: ClickHouse TTL is table-level, not per-tenant; true per-tenant retention for shared tables would require either:
    1) separate tables per tenant (not viable),
    2) per-tenant partitioning (explodes partitions), or
    3) row-level deletes keyed by tenant_id (expensive), or
    4) materialize per-tenant aggregates into a policy-governed store.
  - For v1, we should be explicit: telemetry retention is enforced at the dataset level with tier-based defaults; tenant “retention controls” UI should reflect what is actually configurable.

Recommendation for v1 messaging (align with Product)
- Tenant can configure retention for audit logs and admin activity.
- Telemetry/analytics retention is configurable only for a subset of eligible analytics datasets (and may be bounded by service-level constraints). If we cannot support per-tenant enforcement in shared ClickHouse tables, we must clearly document: “Retention is applied at the dataset level; for Dedicated/Private deployments we can apply tenant-specific settings.”
- Action: sync with Naomi Feldman / Marissa Cole on what the Console should claim for Hosted.

D) Validate reporting queries and dashboards
- Identify dashboards/queries that currently do not constrain time windows (e.g., “last 90 days” is implied but not enforced).
- Update queries to always filter on a bounded time range aligned with maximum retention; otherwise queries will silently change semantics when data ages out.
- Add regression tests:
  - A small golden dataset with partitions beyond TTL, verify that dashboard queries still return correct results for recent windows
  - For billing-adjacent usage: verify daily_usage_agg_v1 matches ledger totals for the overlapping window

E) Observability + safety
- Add metrics:
  - ttl_drop_partitions_total{table}
  - ttl_drop_bytes_total{table}
  - query_missing_partitions_warnings_total (if we add query-side detection)
- Add alerting hooks per monitoring plan (ENG-2944):
  - storage growth anomaly after TTL enablement (indicates TTL not running)
  - elevated merge/load due to TTL misconfiguration
- Rollout plan:
  - Enable TTLs in staging first; verify part drops occur
  - Canary in prod for the noisiest table first (request_events_v2) with conservative TTL (e.g., 30d) and watch load
  - Expand to aggregates after confirming no dashboard regressions

Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Final eligibility list published in this ticket (table-by-table) and mirrored in the data inventory source doc
- [ ] TTL enforcement enabled for all eligible tables in staging and prod (or explicitly excluded with rationale)
- [ ] No ClickHouse cluster stability regressions attributable to TTL merges (validated with SRE)
- [ ] Console-facing queries updated to be time-bounded where necessary; verified in staging
- [ ] Written “known limitations” section for Hosted per-tenant telemetry retention (if applicable), with recommendation for Dedicated/Private

Risks / constraints
- ClickHouse TTL being table-scoped limits true per-tenant retention in multi-tenant shared tables.
- Some trace/span data may include high-cardinality attributes; confirm sanitization before labeling eligible.
- Dropping old partitions can break long-range trend charts if they assume multi-year history; ensure the UI defaults match retention.

Links
- PM initiative: sources/linear/product-management/PM-482.json
- Retention schema work: ENG-2911 / ENG-2912
- Monitoring plan: ENG-2944
- Data inventory (working): sources/google_drive/shared_drives/security-and-compliance/data-inventory-and-retention-sources-sheet.json

Next steps (this week)
1) Mei: post the final eligible table list + proposed default/min/max retention by 2025-02-21
2) Logan/Nadia: confirm which tables are required for cost/usage dashboards vs. internal-only
3) Mei + Sean: align on ClickHouse TTL settings and rollout sequence

---
Updates / comments
2025-02-05 (Mei Lin): Initial inventory done. Confirmed request_events_v2 + error_events_v1 are partitioned by event_date (daily). daily_usage_agg_v1 is partitioned by day. trace_spans_v1 is questionable (attributes include route_params); investigating whether payload-like keys are present.

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): Please avoid row-level TTL. Use part-level TTL only. Also note TTL execution is tied to merges; enabling TTL on the largest table may increase background merge pressure. Recommend canary with conservative settings and watch merge queue + CPU.

2025-02-12 (Nadia Rahman): Billing reconciliation uses ledger tables outside ClickHouse; OK to drop telemetry history as long as Console UI and exports clearly state the window. daily_usage_agg_v1 should remain at least 90 days for enterprise expectations.

2025-02-18 (Mei Lin): Implemented TTL in staging for request_events_v2 (30d) and error_events_v1 (30d). Observed partitions dropping as expected after forcing merge; no elevated load yet. Next: update two dashboard queries that lacked explicit time filters (latency p95 panel + error rate trend).
